subject.title: Feature: Slack workspace file injection + global systemPrompt (parity with Telegram)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a Slack account/global `systemPrompt` config field, and what precedence should it have relative to per-channel prompts, the `*` channel fallback, DMs, MPIM/group DMs, and slash commands?
rationale: The remaining work adds a public Slack config surface; current source shows the workspace-file part is solved generically, while prior merged Slack prompt work deliberately avoided exposing the global/DM prompt shape.

options.title: Define Slack account/global prompt inheritance
options.body: Add a documented account/global Slack prompt field with explicit precedence and tests across normal messages, DMs or MPIMs where supported, and slash commands.

options.title: Keep existing channel and wildcard prompts only
options.body: Close or narrow the request if maintainers decide `channels.slack.channels.*.systemPrompt` and explicit per-channel entries are the intended API.

options.title: Defer until raw-text includes land
options.body: Wait for the generic raw-text include API to settle, then revisit whether Slack still needs a separate account/global inheritance surface.

recommendation.title: Define Slack account/global prompt inheritance
recommendation.body: Add a documented account/global Slack prompt field with explicit precedence and tests across normal messages, DMs or MPIMs where supported, and slash commands.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc supplied the clearest merged Slack prompt-boundary signal and authored the commits that removed the exposed global/DM prompt config from the prior approach.
